transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-03
Start: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Brooks (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Maya Kline (Redwood CSM); Liam Chen, Ava Martinez, Noah Patel, Sofia Rivera (Olympus)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC sync focused on cost/unit economics - tokens per dollar, batching tradeoffs, and caching savings. Agreed next steps: run bench with larger batching, share updated cost spreadsheet, run dedicated latency benchmark.

00:00:12 - Ethan: alright, good morning everyone; um quick roll call?
00:00:24 - Liam: Liam here, Ava, Noah and Sofia on our side.
00:00:28 - Ethan: great. i'll do a quick agenda: cost review, results we ran last week, tuning options (batching, caching, quant), and next steps. priya will cover the perf numbers.
00:01:10 - Priya: cool, so recapping last week's runs: we did hosted inference with r-inf-v2-medium model, quantized int8 variant, and ran two configs - baseline with batch 8 and caching off, and tuned with batch 16 + prefix caching. baseline avg tokens/sec was ~420 tokens/s per GPU, tuned got to ~610 tokens/s. these are rough because our traffic distribution has a lot of short chats which limits batching efficiency.
00:02:05 - Ava: can you say tokens/sec/$ again? that's the part our finance team really wants to see.
00:02:12 - Priya: yeah, for the baseline that converts to about 0.00035 dollars per token at hosted list rates we used for the calc - so roughly cost per 1k tokens around $0.35 with baseline; tuned dropped to about $0.23 per 1k tokens given the higher throughput and caching savings.
00:03:05 - Noah: that delta is significant. what assumptions on cache hit rate did you use? we saw our p99 reuse at like 12% in the stub logs.
00:03:18 - Priya: for the tuned run we used a 25% prefix cache hit assumption - that was optimistic given your sample but the caching engine we used there stores both prefixes and KV segments; if your real workload is 10-12% the savings scale down proportionally.
00:03:42 - Liam: ok we can get you more realistic numbers; i can share a week of anonymized trace that shows exact reuse per route.
00:03:55 - Ethan: perfect, that will help. one note on math: tokens/sec per GPU improved because with larger batch we reduce per-token overhead; cost per token reduces with batching but latency for individual requests increases slightly - tradeoff to watch.
00:04:30 - Sofia: our UX team is sensitive to added latency, p95 can't exceed 300ms for chat. are we seeing p95 impact?
00:04:42 - Priya: with batch 16 on hosted and no dedicated GPU isolation p95 increased from ~220ms to ~320ms in some windows. when we moved to a dedicated capacity profile the p95 dropped back to ~240ms at batch 16 because of predictable throughput. so depending on your SLO you might want Dedicated or lower batch sizes on hosted.
00:05:20 - Ava: can you repeat the dedicated vs hosted cost delta? we need ballpark monthly for a pilot.
00:05:29 - Priya: sure. for a pilot traffic at 10 req/s average and typical sequence length ~80 tokens, hosted list cost projection was ~$9k/month; the Dedicated reserved capacity equivalent (small pool 4 GPUs) with commitment looked closer to $6.5k/month in our model due to better packing and no multi-tenant overhead - but that assumes you can commit and that utilization stays above ~60%.
00:06:10 - Noah: does that include KV cache savings and dedup?
00:06:18 - Priya: yes, the tuned line includes an assumed 20% effective token reduction from caching and a 10% improvement from quantization path. we can break that down in the spreadsheet.
00:06:30 - Ethan: quick interjection: for dedicated deployments there's also networking egress considerations if you run in a VPC or on-prem, and licensing for on-prem can change the unit economics.
00:06:48 - Liam: on egress - we'll probably run in our Azure VNet so egress is internal; but on-prem could be different.
00:06:55 - Priya: got it. also worth calling out that some workloads don't benefit from batching due to interactive patterns; for Qs where users type short prompts, batching hurts latency with little throughput gain. we noticed in your traces a mix: 60% short sessions (<=40 tokens) and 40% longer.
00:07:30 - Sofia: so is prefix KV caching most helpful for longer sequences?
00:07:36 - Priya: yes, longer sequences and repeated system prompts benefit more. if you have repeated templates or reuse across requests caching surfaces bigger wins.
00:07:55 - Ava: security / compliance quick Q: if we go Dedicated, do we still get audit logs and KMS support?
00:08:02 - Maya: yes, Dedicated and Private both integrate with customer KMS and provide audit logs. we'll send SOC2 and KMS integration docs after this call.
00:08:15 - Noah: good. another perf question - when you say quantization contributed 10% improvement, is that tokens/sec or model quality tradeoff?
00:08:25 - Priya: it's tokens/sec / cost improvement; quality delta was negligible for our prompts at int8, but we recommend regression evals before rollouts. Redwood Optimize can run evals against your prompt sets.
00:08:50 - Ethan: quick pause - do we have any blockers this week?
00:08:55 - Liam: only that we need clearer cost breakdown for execs - they want tokens/sec/$ and monthly cost for pilot with both hosted and dedicated options.
00:09:10 - Ethan: understood. we'll send the spreadsheet.
00:09:20 - Priya: demoed a couple of charts: tokens/sec by batch size; marginal cost per 1k tokens vs batch, and cache hit sensitivity curve. (note: brief screen-share referenced)
00:09:45 - Priya: the sensitivity curve shows that at 10% cache hit you save ~7% cost, at 25% you save ~18%. batching from 8->16 gives ~30-40% throughput uplift on average for mixed-length workloads.
00:10:25 - Sofia: can Redwood help us estimate realistic cache hit rates from our traces?
00:10:31 - Priya: yes, if you supply request traces we can run a cache-sim overlay and give predicted effective hit rates and cost savings.
00:10:45 - Ava: we'll send traces but need assurance traces stay private.
00:10:51 - Maya: traces can be uploaded to our private S3 intake or shared via secure link; we sign an NDA for analytics if needed and data is removed after analysis.
00:11:05 - Noah: good. on batching tradeoffs, any thoughts on dynamic batching where small-latency requests are prioritized?
00:11:14 - Priya: Redwood runtime supports latency buckets and dynamic batching - you can pin certain routes to low-latency with smaller batch sizes while letting background routes use large batch sizes. there's also adaptive batching that watches queue times and tunes batch windows.
00:11:45 - Liam: ok that could work. question: our peak is bursty, we worry about cold-starts and token pricing during spikes. how does Redwood handle burst capacity?
00:11:58 - Ethan: two options: Dedicated with burst pool reserve or hosted with autoscale and fallback to smaller, cheaper models if cost becomes a concern. Redwood has configurable burst policies and can route to cheaper variants automatically.
00:12:20 - Priya: we measured cold-start tail latencies and they were much better with a kept-warm pool on Dedicated; hosted had slightly higher tail during rapid scalings.
00:12:34 - Sofia: team asked about model variants - could we route lower-critical routes to a smaller model to save cost?
00:12:40 - Priya: absolutely. routing policies support model families and automatic fallback; you can specify quality thresholds so that only non-core flows use cheaper variants.
00:12:58 - Ethan: jumping to concrete pilot numbers - if we assume your 10 req/s baseline, with caching at 12% and batch 12, pilot hosted est $7.2k/month, dedicated est $6.1k/month with 4-gpu pool and 60% utilization. spreadsheet will show both.
00:13:30 - Ava: thanks. please flag any assumptions clearly.
00:13:34 - Ethan: yes we'll annotate assumptions.
00:13:40 - Priya: small caveat - our tokens/sec numbers assume average sequence length; if your UI changes and length rises, cost moves linearly. also note that embeddings usage and reranking are separate line items.
00:13:58 - Liam: understood - we currently do light embeddings for search, mostly generation for chat.
00:14:08 - Sofia: have you seen any issues with hallucinations when quantized models are used?
00:14:14 - Priya: minor differences in generation surface but not significant for your templates; we always recommend evaluation sets and regen checks during quantized rollout. Redwood Optimize can automate those regression alerts.
00:14:35 - Noah: legal asked about data residency - if we use Private deployment in our VNet does it meet our residency needs for EU customers?
00:14:44 - Maya: yes, Private supports region-specific deployment and data residency controls; we can scope that in contract.
00:14:55 - Ethan: let's talk benchmarks - we should run an end-to-end 90-minute bench with your traffic profile to measure p50/p95 and cost. can we schedule Dec 10?
00:15:05 - Liam: Dec 10 works for us. Ava will be the SRE contact.
00:15:10 - Ava: yep i'll coordinate.
00:15:20 - Priya: action item: i'll run two bench variants before Dec 10 - one with batch 16 + prefix caching on hosted, another on a dedicated small pool with batch 16 and quant int8. i'll post results and perf logs.
00:15:38 - Ethan: great. any more questions from execs?
00:15:45 - Noah: finance will want an easy one-page summary they can present. can you include a one-pager with assumptions and monthly delta?
00:15:52 - Ethan: yes we will.
00:16:00 - Priya: quick note about measurement - tokens/sec/$ we computed using our internal per-GPU throughput model; if you have custom pricing (Azure discounts) share that and we'll re-run the calc.
00:16:20 - Liam: we have EDP discounts; will send unit price.
00:16:27 - Sofia: small technical Q - how does KV cache eviction work for long running sessions?
00:16:33 - Priya: eviction is LRU-ish with TTLs you control. for long-running sessions the cache keeps per-conversation KVs until TTL expires; for very long sessions you can pin conversation KVs or flush on session end.
00:16:55 - Ava: are there any logs we need to wire up for observability?
00:17:00 - Maya: we ship tracing hooks, token-level cost logs, and per-route dashboards. these are configurable in the console; we'll share a sample dashboard link.
00:17:14 - Ethan: wrapping toward next steps - we'll send the spreadsheet and a one-pager, priya will run bench and post results, and maya share SOC2/KMS docs.
00:17:27 - Liam: sounds good.
00:17:35 - Priya: one more point on batching tradeoffs - for UX-sensitive flows try adaptive batching with a 50ms max queue window; it captures some batching benefits without blowing up p95.
00:17:50 - Sofia: ok we'll try that.
00:18:15 - (brief cross-talk about calendar invites, timestamps)
00:18:45 - Ethan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts in the next 24 hours.
00:18:52 - Noah: thanks, bye.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcribe had a few mis-hearings (e.g., r-inf-v2 read as are-inf v2), and some speaker overlaps.

- Ethan: deliver cost spreadsheet and one-pager (12/04)
